speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We found it shocking that demeaning and insulting images of the Prophet should be published anywhere.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These images had led to rioting and deaths in parts of the world, including in France, United Kingdom, Middle East, Africa and Indonesia.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Major media publications including in western countries have refrained from publishing the offensive caricatures.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MUIS determined that these images are offensive to Muslims.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MUIS also said that such content that negatively depicts Islam and Muslims, or any religion for that matter, are not acceptable, and even more so in a multi-religious society such as Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Hence, MUIS supports IMDA’s classification of this book.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I am certain the Muslim community also supports this move.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Beside the caricatures of the Prophet and Islam, the book also included images insulting to other religions.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The authors may say that they do not intend for the publication to be insulting or demeaning, and their intention is to educate, but the Government rejects that.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It is unacceptable to publish such caricatures and insulting images of the Prophet in the name of free speech, academia or otherwise.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I can only imagine the feelings of our people, Muslims and non-Muslims, if such images are allowed to be published in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In our multiracial and multi-religious society, it is vital that we treat every religion with respect and not denigrate religious communities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Instead, we should encourage dialogue and greater understanding among different religious communities, so that we strengthen our social fabric.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The harmonious race and religious relations that we enjoy in Singapore today require constant care and attention of the Government and the society at large.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We do not want to risk anything that will begin unravelling the peace and harmony we enjoy from the due respect and consideration that everyone gives to each other.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We remain committed to working closely with all our religious communities to preserve and strengthen our racial and religious harmony, which is a bedrock of our cohesive society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: (In Malay):   Mr Speaker, the book titled "Red Lines: Political Cartoons and the Struggle Against Censorship" was classified by IMDA as objectionable under the Undesirable Publications Act (UPA) because it contained material that denigrated several religions and religious figures.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS) reviewed the book and found that it contained several caricatures Prophet Muhammad, as well as other important figures that will incite discrimination against Muslims, mocked the Holy Quran and our Prophet, and demeaned Islam.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MUIS determined that these images are offensive to many Muslims.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MUIS also said that such content that negatively depicts Islam and Muslims, or any other religions for that matter, are not acceptable, and even more so in a multireligious society such as Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Hence, MUIS supports IMDA's classification for this book.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I am certain the Muslim community also supports this move.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Aside from caricatures of the Prophet and Islam, the book also contained images that denigrated other religions.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The authors may say that the book is not intended to insult or demean anyone, and instead, their intention is to educate.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Publishing such caricatures and images that insult the Prophet or other religions is unacceptable, even when it is in the name of free speech, academia and so on.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The harmonious race and religious relations that we enjoy in Singapore today can easily unravel and we must give it constant care and attention together.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I fully agree that any insult to religions, especially in Singapore, is unacceptable.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I would just like to ask whether the political nature of the cartoons in the publication has got any part to play in the decision.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Political cartoons are not, in themselves, the problem.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is very clear that "Red Lines" was disallowed for its offensive religious content.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I have spoken about it, Minister Masagos has further elaborated on why these are of great concern in our multicultural, multi-religious context.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They either contained offensive and prejudicial comments about other religions or espoused polemical religious teachings which were likely to cause ill will and hatred amongst the different religious groups in Singapore. "Red Lines" is objectionable for similar reasons.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I think any words or images that are offensive to any religion is hurtful and the hurt remains.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I have two supplementary questions for Minister Masagos.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Given that the content in such publications can be replicated or duplicated and made viral in today's context, what can any members of the public – whether Muslim or otherwise – do to report or express their concerns to MUIS, especially if they feel that certain publications or images would be offensive to any particular group.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: My second question is on the Undesirable Publications Act.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The definition of a publication as "objectionable" is within the context of enmity or hatred between different races or difference religions.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The question is, what about publications that may create hostility within the Muslim community itself?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Would MUIS play a role in the determination of such publications being offensive?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Zhulkarnain's questions are very important and let me address the first part of it first and I think Minister Masagos would probably like to supplement.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Social media platforms have terms of service, community standards as well as feedback mechanisms for users to flag or report inappropriate content.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Local content providers can be required to take down the content.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: IMDA can also direct Internet service providers in Singapore to block access to such websites.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In 2020, not so long ago, there was in fact a Facebook post by the NUS Atheist Society that was highly offensive to both Muslims and Christians.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And so, that stand is very clear and also very consistent.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To Mr Zhulkarnain's other question regarding the role of MUIS.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the case of "Red Lines" and other content related to Islam, IMDA did and continues to seek the views of MUIS.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So you would expect Muslims to react when the Prophet's dignity is conned or when he is really ridiculed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Now, when Muslims are rightfully indignant at any derogatory remarks or insults made of the Prophet, but we must nonetheless, be guided by our prophetic principles of compassion, graciousness and magnanimity.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I say this because the Prophet himself, faced this when he was alive.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In fact, once, when a group of men prayed publicly for death and calamity to befall him, A'ishah, his wife, wanted to do the same thing, to pray for death and calamity for the same people who prayed that on the Prophet.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Prophet stopped her and counselled her that, "Allah, our God, is gentle and he loves gentleness." So, I call upon fellow Muslims to follow what our religion teaches us: To conduct ourselves in the most exemplary way, even when we are rightfully hurt and indignant by the act put against our religion or our Prophet.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Let us live by our laws because we can and where they are such literature that incite or endorse ethnic, racial or religious hatred, strife or intolerance, we will prevent them from happening and from such literatures from being published and distributed in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As mentioned by my colleague, Minister Josephine Teo, members of the public who have concerns on a particular content in publications should inform IMDA, whether it is of one religion to another; persons against another religion; or even within the religion or their community.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: IMDA will always seek input from the relevant agency before it makes its decision on content regulation.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In this example, IMDA had consulted MCCY and MUIS if the Islamic content involved was indeed derogatory, insulting and hurtful and they were so.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, we hope that while we are indignant, we know the the content yet to be distributed are hurtful and derogatory to our religion, to our Prophet, I counsel ourselves, my fellow Muslims in my community, to behave and conduct in the most exemplary way.
